faq.q: What is the sea temperature in Marbella in September?
faq.a: In September, the Mediterranean off Marbella averages 22–24°C. Early in the month it can reach 25°C, making swimming and snorkelling very comfortable. By late September, it cools slightly but remains pleasant for water activities.

faq.q: Is September a good time for a boat rental in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes. September offers warm air and sea temperatures, reduced summer crowds, and generally calm conditions. You'll enjoy longer periods of sunshine and a more relaxed atmosphere in Puerto Banús and along the coast.

faq.q: What should I wear for a September boat trip?
faq.a: Light clothing, swimwear, and a light jacket or windbreaker for the evening. Sunscreen, sunglasses, and a hat are essential. Water shoes are useful if you plan to swim from rocky coves like Cala del Faro.

faq.q: Are there any weather risks in September?
faq.a: September is generally stable, but occasional thunderstorms can occur, especially after a hot spell. Our skippers monitor forecasts closely and will adjust the route or timing if needed. Safety always comes first.

faq.q: Can I swim in the sea in September?
faq.a: Absolutely. The sea is warm and inviting, with visibility often improving after the summer. Many of our charters include stops at coves like Cala Cortés or Cala del Faro, where the water is clear and calm.

faq.q: What is the best time of day for a boat trip in September?
faq.a: Morning departures (around 10:00) offer calm seas and good light. Afternoon trips are warmer and great for swimming. Sunset charters are particularly stunning, with the Sierra Blanca and La Concha glowing in the evening light.

faq.q: Do you offer charters in September despite the season change?
faq.a: Yes. Our fleet operates year-round from Puerto Banús. In September, all boats are available, including the Astondoa 40, Azimut 39, and Mangusta 80. You can book by the hour or for full-day charters.

data.body_html:
September is the sweet spot for a marbella boat rental weather september experience: the summer heat has softened, the water is still bath-warm, and the crowds have thinned. If you're planning a charter from Puerto Banús, you're in for some of the most reliable sea conditions of the year. Here's what to expect, in concrete numbers.

September Sea Conditions: The Numbers

In Marbella, September sea temperatures hover between 22°C and 24°C. Early in the month, you might see 25°C near the surface, especially in shallow coves. Air temperatures range from 26°C to 30°C during the day, dropping to around 20°C in the evening. You'll get roughly 10–11 hours of sunshine per day, with sunset around 20:30 at the start of the month and 19:45 by the end.

Why September Is Ideal for a Boat Charter

The Mediterranean is at its most stable in September. The levante wind (from the east) is lighter than in summer, often dropping to 10–15 knots — perfect for a smooth ride along the coast. Swell rarely exceeds 0.5 metres in the Bay of Marbella, so even guests prone to seasickness find it comfortable. Water clarity improves as plankton levels drop, making snorkelling at Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés particularly rewarding.

What to Expect on the Water

Expect warm, dry days with occasional late-afternoon clouds. Sea breezes keep things pleasant even at midday. You'll see fewer boats than in July or August, meaning more space in anchorages and a quieter vibe at beach clubs like those near Cabopino. The sea is calm enough for water sports — if you charter the Mangusta 80, a jet ski is included free with your 4-hour minimum hire.

Choosing the Right Boat for September

All our fleet is available in September, but here's a quick guide:

  • Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) — great for families, €749/2h or €2,299/8h.
  • Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) — same pricing, ideal for small groups.
  • Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) — luxury with jet ski included, €4,719 for 4h.
  • Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) — a nimble option for a quick spin.
  • Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) — for a grand day out.

For other boats like the Pershing 46 or Lagoon 380, pricing is on request via WhatsApp — just ask.

What's Included in Your Charter

Every charter from our fleet includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). That means no hidden costs — just show up and enjoy. Your skipper will know the best spots for swimming, anchoring, and maybe spotting dolphins.

September Itineraries: Where to Go

From Puerto Banús, you can head east to Cabopino for a quieter anchorage, or west to Estepona and Sotogrande for a longer cruise. A favourite is the trip to Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés — small coves with crystal-clear water. If you want a mix of beach and culture, anchor near the Golden Mile and take a tender to shore for lunch.

Booking Tips for September

September is still a popular month, so book at least a week ahead, especially for weekends. Morning departures (10:00) give you calm seas and the best light. If you prefer a sunset cruise, the light on La Concha is spectacular. Remember: the sea stays warm well into October, so even a late-September charter feels like summer.

What is the sea temperature in Marbella in September?

Morning departures (around 10:00) offer calm seas and good light. Afternoon trips are warmer and great for swimming. Sunset charters are particularly stunning, with the Sierra Blanca and La Concha glowing in the evening light.

Yes. Our fleet operates year-round from Puerto Banús. In September, all boats are available, including the Astondoa 40, Azimut 39, and Mangusta 80. You can book by the hour or for full-day charters.
